issue_context.title: [STJ] NumberHandling property of JsonSerializerOptions is ignored when using json SrcGen
issue_context.body:
### Description

NumberHandling property of JsonSerializerOptions is ignored when using json sourcegenerated `JsonSerializerOptions`, resulting in an exception being thrown.

Exception info:
`System.Text.Json.JsonException: The JSON value could not be converted to System.Double.`

### Reproduction Steps

```json
{
  "gridAcc": [
    109,
    111.0098,
    110.898735,
    110.315788,
    105.692307,
    "NaN",
    "NaN",
    109.071426,
    107.735291,
    110.929581,
    111.216217,
    110.681816
  ]
}
```

```cs
var jsonSerializerOptions = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web) { NumberHandling = JsonNumberHandling.AllowNamedFloatingPointLiterals };
var accuracyTrackerDtoSerializerContext = new AccuracyTrackerDtoSerializerContext(jsonSerializerOptions);

await using var fileStream = File.OpenRead("<path to file containing json above>");
var accuracyTrackerDto = await JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsync(fileStream, accuracyTrackerDtoSerializerContext.AccuracyTrackerDtoWithoutNumberHandlingAttribute, cancellationToken: default).ConfigureAwait(false);

public readonly struct AccuracyTrackerDtoWithoutNumberHandlingAttribute
{
    [JsonPropertyName("gridAcc")]
    public List<double>? GridAcc { get; }

    [JsonConstructor]
    public AccuracyTrackerDtoWithoutNumberHandlingAttribute(List<double>? gridAcc)
    {
        GridAcc = gridAcc;
    }
}

[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<AccuracyTrackerDtoWithoutNumberHandlingAttribute>))]
public partial class AccuracyTrackerDtoSerializerContext : JsonSerializerContext {}
```



### Expected behavior

No exception being thrown and the JSON list being deserialized with NaN values.

### Actual behavior

`System.Text.Json.JsonException` being throw, with the following message:
"The JSON value could not be converted to System.Double. Path: $.gridAcc[5] | LineNumber: 7 | BytePositionInLine: 9."

### Regression?

This issue seemingly could be reproduced on .NET 5, 6 and 7 (by changing the TFM), but should probably be double-checked. 

### Known Workarounds

The bug doesn't occur when the property in the class/struct itself is annotated with the `JsonNumberHandling` attribute, or when not using a `JsonSerializerContext` at all. (See repo linked in the Other Information section)

### Configuration

.NET SDK: 7.0.100

### Other information

Code that can be used to reproduce the issue, as well as the workaround and unaffected path, can be found on the following repo:
https://github.com/ErisApps/STJ_NumberHandling_Bug

@eiriktsarpalis I "solved" this already for my specific scenario by specifying the `JsonNumberHandling` attribute on the affected property (as described as a possible workaround in my initial post), but was puzzled when stumbling upon this... not knowing it was a bug at first.
Thanks for the suggestion though.

review_comments: Should the same check for type infos apply here?

It's causing test failures for cases where you have properties containing POCOs annotated with `JsonNumberHandling.Strict` and you have global configuration specifying `WriteAsString`. The fast-path method cannot pass the property-level configuration to downlevel `JsonSerializer.Serialize` calls so it ends up picking up the global configuration incorrectly. Probably not a super common scenario but I figured we should be conservative for now.
